proof_summary: For \(n\ge100\), let \(d=D(n)\), \(e=D(d)\), and \(T=(n-e)/9\); digit-sum congruences modulo \(9\) and elementary bounds show that \(T\) is integral and long enough to pad the digits of \(d-1\), whose padded block and digitwise \(9\)-complement are then concatenated with a zero and the digits of \(d\). The resulting \(k\) has \(D(k)=9T+e=n\) and is divisible by \(d\), since the complementary blocks represent \(d(10^T-1)\); also \(k\ne n\) because \(D(n)<n\), while explicit witnesses handle \(1\le n<100\).
